findings.summary: Four reciprocal physical effects and a same-trajectory local reduction meet their one-percent comparison targets under one evolving metric and common action.

Historical finite pressure-magnitude crossings and slopes are recorded. Their interpretation as opposing parent-child forces, mechanical balance or a centre-regularity test is withdrawn. The corrected owner defines the remaining diagnostic scope.
Sampled local trapping character on the finite chart. Initial extrema marginal. Explicitly not a global horizon and not a child region.
Completed finite turnover on the frozen depth-three window. Geometry there is an input.

A static local leading-action solution changes its inner and outer proper lengths in opposite directions. A locked first-order forecast predicts the withheld changes with 0.018 and 0.793 percent remainders.
Retained, drive and memory columns reconstruct the field and its full common-action force, evolving their own geometry. Independent full evolution agrees at recorded numerical precision.
Nonperiodic horizon-regular PG exterior with a distinct areal-radius near-throat child. The six-case numerical family stopped without completed case summaries; its physical results are not claimed.

Characteristic coordinate speeds are 1-beta and -1-beta, about -1.1708 and -3.1708 at the throat, both toward the child even when the local normal-frame light direction is outward. The local speed stays one.
Regional eigenvalues are Lambda_n times the shared dimensionless spectrum; coherent nesting holds at arbitrary finite depth by the normalized recursion.
The v7 retained IV preparation defines a unique conditional transfer operator. Its v8 evaluation is recorded separately; remote generation remains open.

Fixed finite IV characteristic data produce a central pulse and positive post-input tail. The sign has a conditional analytic bound; numerical magnitudes have spatial, geometry and independent integral controls. Later persistence and remote preparation remain open.

Complete compatible signed central traces determine a unique preparation in the fixed finite model. Positive compact sources impose additional range restrictions; no second-geometry equivalence or numerical inverse is claimed.

The canonically normalized conformal probe adds no singular scalar surface stress or regular tangential flux jump at the fixed pure-tension wall. This quadratic local compatibility check leaves bulk backreaction, normal-force balance, quantitative amplitude validity and stability open.

The original compact conformal probe forces a quadratic source-leg radius correction at fixed corner geometry and affine normalization. The post-input coefficient and slope are negative, with independent integrated and smooth-exterior frame checks. No mass shift, coupled wall evolution or finite-amplitude error bound is established.

The fixed compact conformal preparation and declared corner data determine a geometric Misner-Sharp mass response along the same initial null leg. Full frame conversion, mixed-radius transport and improved-stress flux agree; the post-input quadratic coefficient is negative and constant. No vacuum future, asymptotic energy, evolved wall response or finite-amplitude bound is established.

The full canonical conformal scalar stress has zero regular normal-stress jump on the fixed transmitting wall at quadratic order. Together with zero additional scalar surface stress and fixed vacuum/tension sources, this requires a vanishing quadratic variation of mean extrinsic-curvature trace. That variation includes bulk metric and wall displacement; no unchanged trajectory, bulk evolution or finite-amplitude validity bound is established.

The fixed leading wall field and quiet anchor determine a conditional quadratic geometric mass functional on the smooth exterior side through both null fluxes and the full conformal endpoint correction. Original-frame improved-stress transport agrees independently. No numerical mass curve, late mass sign or plateau, coupled cap/wall solution, corrected observer response or finite-amplitude bound is established.

Subtracting the fixed cap vacuum at the actual radius gives a conditional cap mass functional. Together with the exterior functional and the shared quiet event, it determines a regular quadratic wall displacement equation; the angular, temporal and normal junction conditions agree with two-sided mass transport. No numerical mass or displacement curve, smooth sourced bulk metric, corrected observer response or finite-amplitude bound is established.

The original prepared scalar drives linear radius and lapse evolution on the genuine initial exterior rectangle. Geometric mass is compared with both independent scalar-flux paths and the integrated null constraints, with separate numerical refinements. The solved transverse leg supports later continuation; the moving-wall strip, cap metric, corrected observer response and finite-amplitude remainder remain open.
